dead-animal-removal.intro: Lake City's dead-animal calls belong to its older housing and its farm-trade history — a Florence County town of pre-war and postwar homes, tobacco warehouses in its past, and the flat Pee Dee countryside around it. The pattern is the region's: raccoons and opossums dead in crawlspaces and wall voids over the winter, discovered by odour in the first warm weeks; squirrels and rats in the attics and walls of the older homes; and the occasional animal in a chimney that announces the flue was uncapped all along. Lake City homes sit largely on piers with vented crawlspaces, and the Lowcountry air does the distribution — one carcass under a house can perfume every room, which is why the call usually comes described as a whole-house emergency rather than a location.
dead-animal-removal.extendedBody:
Location by evidence in a pier-built town

We work Lake City dead-animal calls from the evidence outward. The household's account — when the scratching was last heard, in which wall, on which side — is combined with the fly activity at the vents and the staining at the foundation to place the search, and then the crawlspace is walked completely, because the carcass in a vented footprint is often two rooms away from the smell's worst room. Wall voids are opened at the carcass, located by probe and evidence, never by demolition. Removal is sealed and complete, the void treated, and the entry — the failed vent screen, the foundation gap, the uncapped flue — identified and quoted for closing while we are there. In a town of Lake City's housing age, the entry is never a surprise and never unique; the honest measure of the visit is whether the next animal finds the address closed.

faqs.q: How much does dead animal removal cost in Lake City?
faqs.a: It depends on where the animal is — crawlspace removals are the straightforward end; a carcass sealed in a wall void or an uncapped chimney is slower, more precise work. We locate it first, then price the removal before opening anything, so the quote is for a known job. The entry inspection is included in the visit, and closing the entry is quoted separately and plainly — in older Lake City housing, that closing is usually the difference between one call and an annual one.

faqs.q: Something died in our Lake City chimney — we think. How is that handled?
faqs.a: Chimney carcasses — raccoons and squirrels, most often — are located from the top and the cleanout, and removed through whichever access does the least harm to the flue. The smell in a chimney case concentrates at the fireplace and worsens when the house is closed up, which matches most accounts we hear. Once it is out, the flue gets the conversation it has needed: a proper cap, because an uncapped chimney in this county is a den application form, and the next tenant — alive, with kits, in the spring — is a considerably bigger job than the cap.
